rationale: Both candidates independently trace the same core live defect the ground-truth reviewer's 0.2-default caveat implies (the model-specific 0.17 threshold never reaches users because AsyncOmniEngine injects 0.2 before TeaCacheConfig resolves), and both explicitly flag that the committed e2e smoke test never asserts an actual cache hit, echoing the reviewer's own words almost verbatim. Y goes further with a rigorously computed finding (the calibrated polynomial is near-constant and non-monotone over its own calibration range, undermining TeaCache's adaptivity) and keeps every other finding tightly grounded in diff-touched files with verified evidence, giving it stronger precision and cleaner, more actionable prose. X has comparable depth but drifts into speculative 'major' claims about quality_policy.py/Cache-DiT interactions in files outside the diff with a hedged, unverifiable buildkite-CI finding, and its evidence-dump formatting is harder to act on. Neither review contains a LATENT GAP CHECK section.
